The hybrid search returned txn-reject-01, a nearly identical case involving the same sender account (ACC-4001), same recipient (ACC-4090 / QuickGadgets Online), similar amount (2100 USD vs. 1980 USD here), and identical fraud indicators: card-not-present charge to unrecognized overseas merchant immediately following unusual/foreign login. Osei, ACC-4001) all rejected as confirmed fraud for card-not-present overseas purchases with disputed charges. The fund-tracing signal is clean (no circular flow, layering, or mule patterns detected). The amount is moderate but consistent with fraudster testing patterns before larger transfers. The convergence of sender identity, merchant profile, unusual login triggering the charge, and cardholder dispute all point to unauthorized account access.
